doc.title: Joe LaBarbera interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 15, 2021

title: Old itineraries and the grind of Woody's touring
summary: He still has his Woody Herman itineraries, packed with day-in day-out dates.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Did you save your calendars from those days?
I’ve got a couple of itineraries, yeah.

Yeah. Sometimes you open it up and you look back, it’s like, oh I remember that gig, I remember that club and I remember that road — how tough — it’s funny what we remember about gigs sometimes it’s not the music, sometimes it’s how many stairs do I have to go up.

Well as you mentioned previously, my Woody Herman itinerary, I’ve still got a few of those, and they are packed. I mean it’s day-in, day-out. I mean you had to do that in order to just pay for the band and pay for the bus. You had to work every day.
